commons.title: SEA Chinese origin map PNG.png
commons.description:
Previously published by me in jpg format at File:SEA Chinese origin map.jpg
Source:**
Cities: adapted from Backman, Michael (1995). Overseas Chinese Business Networks in Asia. Parkes, ACT: East Asia Analytical Unit, Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade. ISBN 0-642-22960-0. - Some city names changed to match modern spellings. - Lehui and Jiongdong no longer exist today, instead being part of Qionghai county. - Jieyang was a mistake in the book, adapted from “Chan, K.B. and C.Chiang, “Stepping Out: The Making of Chinese Entrepreneurs” , Prentice Hall, Singapore, 1994”, which was adapted from “Cheng, L.K., “Social Change and the Chinese in Singapore: A Socio-Economic Geography With Special Reference to Bāng Structure”, Singapore University Press, Singapore, 1985”. The city in question is likely supposed to be Quanzhou.
Languages:
Mainland China:
- Hokkien, Teochew, Henghua(Pu-Xian): Wikimedia commons File:Min dialect map.svg (citing Language Atlas of China, by Stephen Adolphe, Li Rong, Theo Baumann, and Mei W. Lee, Longman, 1987, ISBN 978-962-359-085-3, map B8.)
- Hainanese: Wurm, Stephen Adolphe; Li, Rong, eds. (1987). "Map B12: Min Supergroup (Fujian, Taiwan, Eastern Guangdong and Hainan Island) (闽语)". Language Atlas of China (中国语言地图集). Hong Kong: Longman Group (Far East) Ltd. Sheet B12. ISBN 978-962-359-085-3.
- Fuzhounese, Hokchia(Fuqing): Wikimedia commons File:Fuzhou language map.jpg
- Tingzhou Hakka, Yue-Tai Hakka: Wurm, Stephen Adolphe; Li, Rong, eds. (1987). "Map B15: Hakka Group (客家话)". Language Atlas of China (中国语言地图集). Hong Kong: Longman Group (Far East) Ltd. Sheet B15. ISBN 978-962-359-085-3.
- Hailu Hakka: Li, Rong; Zhang, Jiarong, eds. (2012). "Map B1-17: Hakka Dialect: Jiangxi, Hunan, Fujian, Guangdong, Hong Kong, Taiwan (B1-17 客家话)". Language Atlas of China (中国语言地图集) (2nd ed.). Beijing: Commercial Press. Sheet B1-17. ISBN 978-7-100-07054-6. (Hailu Hakka is not mapped in the 1st edition)
- Cantonese, Taishanese: Wikimedia commons File:Ping and Yue dialect map.svg (citing map B8 of the Language Atlas of China, by Stephen Adolphe, Li Rong, Theo Baumann, and Mei W. Lee, Longman, 1987, ISBN 978-962-359-085-3.) Guangfu and Siyi are mapped as Cantonese and Taishanese respectively, which are their prestigious forms.
Taiwan:
- Hokkien: Wikimedia commons File:Taiwanese Hokkien Map.svg (citing 《台灣的語種分布與分區》, 洪惟仁, 2013)
- Hakka (Western coast): https://blog.udn.com/Taillywang/156353522
- Hakka (Eastern coast): Wikimedia commons File:Taiwanese Hakka usage map in 2010.svg. Mapping proportion of residents aged 6 or older using Hakka at home in Taiwan in 2010. (citing 2010 polulation and housing census by DGBAS, Executive Yuan.). Hakka is included in the map if the percentage of Hakka spoken is more than 50%.

- Penghu county, Green island, and Orchid island: Wikimedia commons File:Taiwanese Hokkien Map.svg (citing 《台灣的語種分布與分區》, 洪惟仁, 2013) shows that Hokkien is the majority spoken language on Penghu county and Green island, but not Orchid island. Wikimedia commons File:Taiwanese Hakka usage map in 2010.svg. (citing 2010 polulation and housing census by DGBAS, Executive Yuan.) also proves that Hakka is not spoken to a significant degree on either of the three islands.
commons.editorial_reason: A regional language/origin map, not a visible cultural practice or object.
